new.s: What was the official name of the Narasimham Committee set up in 1991?
new.x: The 1991 Narasimham Committee was the Committee on the Financial System; the 1998 one was the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.
new.angle: U0529 PYQ yeeaaddffdb8 #11 1991 committee -> official title

new.s: Who was the chairman of the Committee on the Financial System set up in 1991?
new.x: The Committee on the Financial System (1991) was headed by M. Narasimham, a former RBI Governor.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Narasimham Committee of 1991 was officially called the Committee on the Financial System.
2. The Narasimham Committee of 1998 was officially called the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Narasimham-I (1991) was the Committee on the Financial System and Narasimham-II (1998) the Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.
new.angle: U0529 #11 Narasimham I and II -> official titles

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks:
1. A Regional Rural Bank is sponsored by a commercial bank.
2. The Central Government holds a 50% share in Regional Rural Banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Each RRB is sponsored by a commercial bank, and the Centre keeps its 50% share even after consolidation.
new.angle: U0529 PYQ yf7a36a64a0f RRB -> nature and ownership

new.s: Which of the following holds the largest share in the capital of a Regional Rural Bank?
new.x: The Central Government holds 50% of RRB capital; the sponsor bank and the State hold the rest.

new.s: What does the leverage ratio under Basel III measure?
o: Tier 1 capital against total non-risk-weighted exposure
Stable funding available over one year
new.x: The leverage ratio is Tier 1 capital divided by total exposure that is not risk-weighted; it caps lending against own capital.
new.angle: U0529 #1 Basel III -> leverage ratio meaning

new.s: What is the minimum leverage ratio prescribed by the RBI for banks other than D-SIBs?
new.x: The RBI prescribes a 4% leverage ratio for D-SIBs and 3.5% for other banks; the BCBS minimum is 3%.
new.angle: U0529 #9 leverage ratio -> RBI vs BCBS

new.s: Which ratio is used as a standard measure of the strength of a bank's balance sheet against its risk-weighted assets?
new.x: CRAR is capital divided by risk-weighted assets and measures the strength of banks' balance sheets.
new.angle: U0529 PYQ yc13447566ba CRAR -> what it measures

new.s: On the recommendation of which committee was the Banks Board Bureau set up?
new.x: The P.J. Nayak Committee (2014) on governance of bank boards proposed the Banks Board Bureau, which began in April 2016.
new.angle: U0529 #17 Banks Board Bureau -> P.J. Nayak

new.s: What was the main function of the Banks Board Bureau?
o: Selecting chairmen and whole-time directors of public sector banks
new.x: The Banks Board Bureau selected PSB chairmen and whole-time directors and boards of PSU insurers and FIs.

new.s: What is the full form of EASE in the context of public sector bank reforms?
o: Easy Access to Savings and Equity
new.x: EASE stands for Enhanced Access and Service Excellence, the reform agenda for PSBs launched in 2017.

new.s: What does the EASE Index measure?
o: Performance of public sector banks on reforms
Ease of doing business for MSMEs
new.x: The EASE Index benchmarks and ranks public sector banks on reform performance; it does not measure MSME ease of doing business.
new.angle: U0529 #15 EASE Index -> what it measures

new.s: Which of the following were among the new private sector banks that entered after the 1991 reforms?
o: Bank of Baroda and Vijaya Bank
new.x: Private bank entry was a post-1991 reform; HDFC and ICICI banks came up by 1995, while the others are nationalised banks.
new.angle: U0529 #5 post-1991 reforms -> private bank entry

new.s: With which subject is the Janakiraman Committee associated?
new.x: The Janakiraman Committee looked into the stock market scam; Goiporia dealt with customer service and Goswami with industrial sickness.

new.s: Which committee dealt with industrial sickness?
new.x: The Onkar Goswami Committee dealt with industrial sickness; Abid Hussain dealt with de-reservation of SSI items.

new.s: Which is the world's oldest international financial organisation?
new.x: The BIS, set up in 1930 at Basel, is the oldest international financial organisation; the IMF and World Bank came in 1944-45.

new.s: In which year was the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) set up?
new.x: The DICGC was formed in 1978 by merging the Deposit Insurance Corporation (1962) and the Credit Guarantee Corporation.

new.s: What is the deposit insurance cover given by the DICGC per depositor per bank?
new.x: Since Budget 2020-21 the DICGC covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, up from ₹1 lakh.

new.s: After how long an overdue period does a loan become a Non-Performing Asset in India?
new.x: A loan becomes an NPA when its interest or principal stays overdue for more than 90 days.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A loan becomes an NPA when its interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
2. An SMA-2 account, overdue for 61-90 days, is classified as an NPA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The NPA cut-off is more than 90 days; SMA-2 accounts (61-90 days) are still standard assets.
